It coincided with the [[2004 United States presidential election|re-election]] of President [[George W. Bush]] as well as many [[2004 United States Senate elections|Senate elections]] and [[2004 United States gubernatorial elections|gubernatorial elections]]. Prior to the election in the [[108th United States Congress|108th Congress]], [[United States Republican Party|Republicans]] held 227 seats, [[United States Democratic Party|Democrats]] held 205, with two [[United States Republican Party|Republican]] vacancies and one independent. As a result of this election, the [[109th United States Congress|109th Congress]] began composed of 232 [[United States Republican Party|Republicans]], 201 [[United States Democratic Party|Democrats]], one independent (who caucuses with the Democrats), and one vacancy (Democrat [[Bob Matsui]] won reelection but died just two days before the beginning of the 109th Congress). Democrats won open seats in [[#Colorado|Colorado]], [[#South Dakota|South Dakota]], and [[#New York|New York]] while ousting incumbents in [[#Georgia|Georgia]] and [[#Illinois|Illinois]]. Republicans won an open seat in [[Kentucky]] while ousting an incumbent in [[2004 United States House of Representatives elections in Indiana|Indiana]]. They gained five seats in [[2004 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas|Texas]] after a controversial [[2003 Texas redistricting|mid-decade redistricting]] placed several rural Democratic incumbents into new districts. Two seats in [[#Louisiana|Louisiana]] swapped party control. {{As of|2025}}, this is the last election in which someone who was not from the [[United States Democratic Party|Democratic]] or [[United States Republican Party|Republican]] parties was elected to the House (Independent [[Bernie Sanders]]). Republicans would not make consecutive net gains in the House (after gaining seats in the [[2002 United States House of Representatives elections|2002 election]]) until [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections|2020]] and [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|2022]].
